overview: The two fundamental performance metrics of any diagnostic test, describing how well it detects disease versus how well it rules it out.
genZNote: Sensitivity: don't miss the sick (rules out disease when negative). Specificity: don't falsely flag the healthy (rules in disease when positive).

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The proportion of people with the disease who correctly test positive (true positive rate).
aspects.valueB: The proportion of people without the disease who correctly test negative (true negative rate).

aspects.label: Clinical Use Case
aspects.valueA: A highly sensitive test is preferred for screening, to minimize missed cases (few false negatives).
aspects.valueB: A highly specific test is preferred for confirmation, to minimize falsely diagnosing healthy people (few false positives).

aspects.label: Mnemonic / Relationship
aspects.valueA: "SnNout" — a highly SeNsitive test, when Negative, rules OUT disease.
aspects.valueB: "SpPin" — a highly SPecific test, when Positive, rules IN disease.

aspects.label: Trade-off Consideration
aspects.valueA: Increasing sensitivity (e.g. lowering a cutoff) often decreases specificity, and vice versa.
aspects.valueB: Increasing specificity often decreases sensitivity — the two must be balanced based on test purpose.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Ability to correctly identify those with disease.
aspects.valueB: Ability to correctly identify those without disease.
